explanations: There is no defect. The message is acked only after every follower page has been written, so a crash mid-fanout leaves it unacked and it is redelivered. Redelivery re-inserts pages already written, but insertMany upserts on (userId, postId), so repeats are harmless. Failures are nacked with capped exponential backoff, and once deliveryCount reaches maxDeliveries the message is dead-lettered rather than retried forever. stop() waits for the loop, which finishes the in-flight batch before returning.

ack is called only after the do/while loop finishes, so the message is still unacked when the process dies and gets redelivered. The cursor lives only in a local variable, so fanout starts again from page one. insertMany upserts on (userId, postId), so those repeat writes do not create duplicates. Nothing saves the cursor, and nothing dead-letters a message because of a partial write.

The check is deliveryCount >= maxDeliveries, so deliveries 1 to 4 are nacked with a delay of 1000 * 2^deliveryCount (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, all under the 60s cap). On delivery 5 the check is true and the message is dead-lettered with the error as the reason. It never retries forever, does not dead-letter on the first failure, and does not drop the message silently.

handle is started for every message in the batch at once, and run() awaits Promise.all before calling receive again. So the nine others run in parallel and finish quickly, but no new work is pulled until the slow fanout completes; concurrency is bounded by batchSize. The 20,000 ms passed to receive is a long-poll wait for new messages, not a timeout on handling.
